column1: # Case|Competing diagnosis A|Competing diagnosis B|Competing diagnosis C|Incorrect repair A|Incorrect repair B|Incorrect repair C

1|The script cannot print to stdout.|The scheduler never starts the script.|The backup destination is healthy and the failure is cosmetic.|Append another success message after the backup.|Ignore the backup exit code and retry the entire host reboot.|Always return zero so downstream jobs continue.

2|The package is installed but the network port is blocked.|The Python source needs executable permission to import packages.|The requests package is part of every Python standard library.|Install the dependency only into the interactive shell interpreter.|Copy the entire system site-packages directory without resolving versions.|Replace the import with a blanket exception handler that reports success.

3|The check completed successfully but the merge button is cached.|The branch lacks a deployment secret.|The repository must be public to report checks.|Disable the required check instead of fixing its trigger.|Run the required check only after merging to main.|Rename the job without updating the required check configuration.

4|The browser cached an expired TLS certificate.|The backend database has exhausted its connection pool.|The upstream is healthy but Nginx worker counts are too low.|Restart Nginx repeatedly without changing its upstream port.|Change the backend hostname while keeping the wrong port.|Increase proxy timeout to hide a refused TCP connection.

5|Apache cannot resolve the upstream hostname.|The site is missing a TLS intermediate certificate.|A browser cache is preventing authorization.|Recursively grant world-write filesystem permissions.|Disable authorization for every virtual host.|Increase the response timeout without changing the deny rule.

6|All application servers ran out of disk at exactly the same time.|The client DNS cache selects the wrong public IP.|HAProxy is refusing valid user credentials.|Disable backend health checks permanently.|Increase the failure threshold while retaining the removed path.|Scale all servers without correcting the health-check contract.

7|The authoritative zone was never updated.|The remaining TTL is a TCP connection timeout.|The recursive resolver must ignore cached records whenever an IP changes.|Change the authoritative record repeatedly to force recursive refresh.|Raise the TTL immediately and promise instant propagation.|Restart the web application to clear every client's DNS cache.

8|The server's application process is not listening.|The private key must be placed in the client trust store.|The client must trust every self-signed leaf certificate.|Disable client certificate verification.|Serve the root CA alone without the missing intermediate.|Replace the hostname with an IP and ignore identity checks.

9|The service exceeded its HTTP response timeout.|The systemd log retention setting is too low.|The executable ran successfully but returned no output.|Restart the missing executable in a tight loop.|Mark the unit successful without running its process.|Increase startup timeout while retaining the invalid path.

10|Compose requires host networking for database connections.|The db service name can be resolved only from the Docker host.|The application container shares the database's loopback interface.|Keep localhost and expose the database publicly.|Use the host's loopback address from inside the isolated app container.|Hardcode an ephemeral container IP into the application image.

11|The application's HTTP port is not published.|SELinux is disabled and therefore blocking labels.|The container cannot resolve the volume's DNS name.|Disable SELinux globally.|Grant world-write permissions while ignoring the label denial.|Run every container privileged to bypass labeling design.

12|The base image has an invalid registry signature.|The runtime container has no exposed port.|The artifact exists inside the image but is hidden by its tag.|Rename the image tag without changing the excluded context.|Disable BuildKit while leaving dist excluded.|Copy the artifact after deployment into a manually modified running container.

13|ECR image tags expire after twelve hours.|The Docker image's ENTRYPOINT expired.|The registry's DNS record must match the IAM username.|Reuse the expired token indefinitely.|Make the private repository public to bypass authentication.|Embed a long-lived administrator access key in the image.

14|The image architecture must match the GitHub account type.|Package writes require all repository branches to be public.|The registry hostname must be added to /etc/hosts.|Grant organization administrator permissions to every job.|Retry the same token without granting required package permission.|Disable package access restrictions for all users.

15|The Jenkinsfile syntax is valid only on the controller.|The build is waiting for Docker image scanning results.|The artifact repository has no free storage.|Remove the agent constraint and run privileged builds on the controller.|Rename an unrelated incompatible agent to satisfy the label.|Increase checkout timeout without providing an executor.

16|The cloud session expired before the workflow began.|The job requires a repository deploy key instead of OIDC.|The cloud role needs unrestricted administrator permissions.|Store permanent cloud administrator keys in the workflow file.|Widen the cloud role trust to every repository.|Retry the login action without enabling token requests.

17|The secret value was deleted from all environments.|The runner needs a public IP to receive variables.|Protected variables are automatically available to every branch.|Unprotect the production credential for all feature branches.|Echo every CI variable to diagnose the missing value.|Copy production secrets into untrusted pipeline artifacts.

18|The deployed artifact has an invalid checksum.|The pipeline needs an unprotected environment name.|A waiting approval is proof of runner CPU exhaustion.|Remove environment checks to release immediately.|Approve the release using a shared approver credential.|Recreate the environment without its approval policy.

19|The context variable names have invalid capitalization.|The build executor cannot access its root filesystem.|The deployment target has run out of disk.|Remove every context restriction.|Copy restricted context values into public project variables.|Run the deployment as a random repository contributor.

20|The compiled artifact lacks Unix execute permission.|The JVM cannot find its DNS resolver.|The application needs a larger heap to read bytecode.|Increase heap memory without changing Java compatibility.|Change only the artifact filename to advertise Java 17 support.|Disable runtime error reporting and keep the incompatible bytecode.

21|The source repository needs a larger Git clone depth.|Gradle cannot compile from a clean checkout by design.|The application runtime port differs between local and CI.|Always install the newest global Gradle release in CI.|Delete the wrapper so developers choose their own version.|Change only the CI timeout without aligning build versions.

22|The registry never allows repeatable dependency resolution.|The package script must run as root.|Node's HTTP keepalive causes dependency version drift.|Delete the lockfile before every CI install.|Use an unpinned latest dependency set for each release.|Copy an arbitrary developer's node_modules into production.

23|The repository cannot accept JAR files.|The token has expired because the version already exists.|Release repositories require overwriting old checksums.|Disable immutability and overwrite the published release.|Delete the existing release used by consumers.|Reuse the same release version with a different filename only.

24|The package format is unsupported by every repository.|The valid token must have administrator access to publish.|The upload timeout caused an authorization decision.|Grant administrator access to the whole platform.|Publish anonymously into the protected repository.|Retry with the same insufficient permissions indefinitely.

25|The remote state lock is always stale after five minutes.|The plan's resource count exceeds the lock limit.|State locking prevents all future successful applies.|Force-unlock while the legitimate apply is running.|Delete the remote state object to bypass its lock.|Disable locking and run both applies concurrently.

26|The backend is corrupt because staging resources exist.|Every workspace intentionally refers to the same desired resources.|The provider cannot read production resources without destroying staging.|Apply the staging plan and rename resources afterward.|Delete the staging state to force production discovery.|Reuse the old plan after switching environment variables.

27|CloudFormation exports are invalid across any stacks.|The importing stack must be deleted regardless of its resources.|The producer's execution timeout is too short.|Force removal of the export before migrating consumers.|Delete the consumer stack without a dependency review.|Rename the export and assume existing imports update automatically.

28|Pulumi stacks disappear whenever a CLI is upgraded.|The cloud provider deletes resources when the backend changes.|The stack needs a new name to recover its old state automatically.|Create an empty replacement stack and apply over existing resources.|Destroy the apparently missing stack's resources manually.|Copy unrelated state into the wrong backend.

29|Ansible deliberately duplicates every line on repeated runs.|The target machine's clock is causing the append.|A changed result proves every shell operation is idempotent.|Ignore the changed result while continuing to append duplicates.|Delete the whole configuration file before every append.|Add retries to the same non-idempotent append command.

30|The generated image must use a public IP after it is built.|SSH authentication is the only possible cause of a routing timeout.|Packer builders cannot run in private subnets.|Open SSH to the whole Internet without creating a valid route.|Disable host-key checks to repair missing network reachability.|Retry SSH indefinitely from the unreachable runner.

31|An identity allow always overrides every explicit deny.|The IAM role session name does not match the S3 bucket name.|The policy JSON must be reordered to place allow first.|Add another broad identity-policy allow without addressing the SCP.|Use a permanent root key to evade policy review.|Remove organization controls globally for the deployment.

32|A healthy instance status guarantees SSH reachability.|The SSH username determines the permitted network source.|The instance needs an unrestricted outbound rule for inbound SSH.|Allow SSH from the entire Internet as the permanent repair.|Reboot the healthy host without changing the blocked access path.|Replace the instance key pair to fix a source-IP mismatch.

33|The NAT gateway must be assigned to every instance's network interface.|Private instances need public inbound SSH to make outbound HTTPS requests.|The subnet's DHCP lease is the only possible outbound dependency.|Assign public IPs and broad inbound access to every private workload.|Change only the application DNS setting without the required route.|Add an Internet-gateway route while leaving private instances without public addressing.

34|The ALB's certificate expired inside the target instance.|The application cannot serve traffic because the target's hostname differs from its tag.|Healthy targets must use port 80 regardless of their application.|Disable target health evaluation permanently.|Change application TLS ciphers without correcting the health-check port.|Increase unhealthy thresholds while checking the wrong port.

35|A maximum size of four still permits eight desired instances.|The scaling policy's CPU metric is a security-group rule.|Every scale-out is blocked by DNS TTL.|Repeat the scale request without reviewing the maximum.|Remove all maximum limits without quota or downstream review.|Add instances manually outside the group's lifecycle as the permanent scaling policy.

36|A bucket policy allow overrides every public-access block.|S3 public access requires disabling encryption.|The object key's file extension controls authorization.|Disable account-wide Block Public Access for every bucket.|Publish the bucket's write permissions to anonymous users.|Make copies of protected objects in an unreviewed public bucket.

37|Every database connection rejection means storage is full.|Application replica count cannot affect aggregate connection count.|An application connection pool is unlimited by database configuration.|Increase every application's pool size to reduce connection failures.|Retry opening database connections without backoff at unlimited concurrency.|Raise the database limit without assessing memory or aggregate pool demand.

38|A local success proves all external health probes are allowed.|Route 53 health checks originate from the application's loopback address.|The DNS record's TTL controls whether a firewall accepts a probe.|Disable all firewall rules to allow any inbound traffic.|Check only the loopback endpoint and ignore external failures.|Mark the endpoint healthy manually without repairing probe access.

39|Lambda concurrency never affects database connection demand.|Each invocation can open unlimited database sessions without resource use.|A database connection limit is controlled by the Lambda package size.|Increase function concurrency without a downstream capacity review.|Open a new database connection for each retry without reuse.|Remove database connection limits and assume memory will scale automatically.

40|CloudWatch automatically copies every metric into every region.|The alarm cannot watch a metric until the application is restarted.|Alarm notification permissions change the region of metric storage.|Treat missing data as healthy without correcting the region.|Duplicate the application to every region to satisfy the wrong alarm.|Rename the metric without aligning its region and dimensions.

41|IRSA trust depends only on the pod's image tag.|An identity-policy allow overrides a mismatched STS trust subject.|Every service account in an EKS cluster shares the same subject.|Trust all Kubernetes service accounts instead of the intended subject.|Embed static IAM keys in the pod specification.|Change only the role's resource permissions without fixing its trust.

42|A reachable registry guarantees image-pull authorization.|The pod's application secret automatically grants the node registry access.|AKS must make every private image public to pull it.|Grant pull access to an unrelated deployment identity only.|Publish the image publicly to bypass the cluster's identity problem.|Give every cluster identity registry administrator access.

43|A successful sign-in grants access to every vault secret.|Key Vault management-plane read permission always includes secret values.|Secret names are case-sensitive role assignments.|Grant broad subscription owner permissions for a secret read.|Switch the vault's permission model without a migration review.|Expose secret values in deployment output to avoid data-plane access.

44|A healthy agent automatically invents data collection rules.|The workspace must share the VM's hostname to collect logs.|The agent's process ID determines its data destination.|Reinstall the healthy agent repeatedly without associating a rule.|Create an unrelated workspace and assume the VM automatically selects it.|Disable log filtering globally instead of assigning the intended collection rule.

45|GKE service-account names need only match by short name across namespaces.|A Kubernetes token automatically grants all Google service-account permissions.|Every pod must use a downloadable Google service-account key.|Distribute permanent cloud service-account keys to every pod.|Bind all namespaces to the privileged cloud identity.|Change only image-pull permissions without fixing workload impersonation.

46|Artifact Registry uses one interchangeable hostname for every location.|Repository-not-found always means the access token expired.|Image tags determine the repository's cloud project automatically.|Create duplicate registries in arbitrary locations to match the wrong URL.|Retry the same incorrect hostname with broader credentials.|Retag the image without correcting its project and location path.

47|The scheduler refuses the pod's resource requests.|A missing registry tag proves the image-pull secret expired.|CrashLoopBackOff and ImagePullBackOff have identical causes.|Restart the pod repeatedly while retaining the absent tag.|Increase container memory to make the missing manifest appear.|Disable image verification and pull a random public replacement.

48|A Pending pod is already using more RAM than its limit.|The scheduler ignores resource requests when a node has low actual usage.|Container logs always explain unscheduled pod capacity.|Delete all memory requests without reviewing actual requirements.|Restart the scheduler instead of addressing capacity.|Force placement onto a full node without a resource safety review.

49|Helm merges an omitted production values file automatically.|The Deployment cannot change replica count after installation.|Chart version numbers override every explicit value.|Scale the live Deployment manually and leave the release values wrong.|Edit the packaged chart inside a running pod.|Use the default values and increase rollout timeout.

50|Every Argo CD diff proves the image is unavailable.|The Kubernetes API cannot store annotations.|An operator-owned annotation means all resource changes should be ignored.|Ignore all differences on the entire Deployment.|Disable drift detection for every application.|Repeatedly patch the generated annotation against its owning controller.

51|Flux cannot use nested directories in a Git repository.|A missing path proves the Git authentication token expired.|Kustomizations always reconcile the oldest fetched revision.|Create an unrelated empty directory on the controller pod.|Widen source credentials instead of correcting the path.|Suspend reconciliation permanently while leaving the source path invalid.

52|Kustomize image names match any substring of an image reference.|An image transformer can change only a container's display name.|The cluster rewrites approved digests back to old tags automatically.|Manually edit the live image while leaving rendered output stale.|Change only the newTag field while keeping the mismatched image name.|Delete the Deployment and redeploy the same incorrect render.

53|Prometheus can scrape any HTTP path without configuration.|A target down status proves the application uses too much memory.|The exporter cannot emit metrics over HTTP.|Mark the target healthy using a recording rule without a successful scrape.|Increase the scrape timeout while retaining the missing endpoint.|Remove the target from monitoring to make the dashboard green.

54|An empty Grafana panel proves Prometheus has no metrics.|Dashboard time ranges automatically rename namespace labels.|Namespace label values are matched by fuzzy similarity.|Relabel every production metric to satisfy one mistaken dashboard filter.|Remove all panel filters and present mixed-environment data as production.|Increase dashboard refresh rate without correcting the query.

55|Alertmanager replicas deduplicate without communicating.|Every duplicate page proves the alert expression is wrong.|The firewall can block cluster peers without affecting notifications.|Disable notification delivery on both replicas.|Delete all alert rules to stop duplicate pages.|Silence every production alert instead of repairing peer coordination.

56|Request IDs always make good low-cardinality index labels.|Adding collector memory alone removes unbounded stream growth.|Loki stores all labels as unindexed raw text.|Add customer IDs and timestamps as more indexed labels.|Keep request_id indexed and disable ingestion failure alerts.|Drop every log line rather than changing the high-cardinality label.

57|A yellow cluster means its primary shards are all unavailable.|A replica can always share the same node as its primary.|Every one-node cluster can provide node-failure redundancy.|Force a replica onto the same node as its primary.|Delete the healthy primary shards to clear the warning.|Disable allocation safeguards and claim full redundancy on one node.

58|A parsing failure proves the source stopped emitting logs.|Grok automatically recognizes every future application format.|An HTTP upstream timeout changes Logstash field names.|Drop every event tagged with a parser failure.|Strip the failure tag without extracting the required fields.|Restart the pipeline repeatedly with the unchanged pattern.

59|A full exporter queue proves no spans are being created.|Telemetry buffers can grow without a memory limit.|Backend latency cannot affect collector memory or drops.|Make the export queue unbounded.|Retry every rejected batch immediately without backoff.|Disable drop metrics while preserving the overloaded export path.

60|Every service is expected to generate an unrelated trace for one request.|Jaeger groups spans solely by matching service names.|Longer retention automatically joins disconnected trace IDs.|Rename downstream service spans without propagating context.|Force every request to use one global trace ID.|Increase trace retention while leaving outbound context absent.

61|Finding vulnerabilities always makes Trivy exit nonzero by default.|A green pipeline proves the image has no findings.|Scanner output severity changes the image's cryptographic signature.|Ignore scanner exit status and grep only for the word complete.|Suppress all critical findings without review.|Publish a green scan badge while leaving deployment ungated.

62|Submitting analysis is equivalent to passing the quality gate.|A failed gate is automatically enforced by every deployment tool.|The production rollout must finish before gate evaluation can start.|Deploy immediately after submitting the analysis request.|Replace the failed gate with an unconditional success step.|Disable quality-gate checks for the main branch.

63|A root-manifest scan automatically covers every nested project.|The dependency is safe because its service directory is not scanned.|A monorepo's security scope is determined by its Git branch name.|Scan only the root manifest and declare every service clean.|Exclude nested projects to improve scanner speed.|Remove the vulnerable service from the report without inspecting its dependencies.

64|Deleting a secret from the latest file revokes the credential.|A merged token is safe if the repository is not advertised.|A scanner finding changes the token's validity automatically.|Delete the line and continue using the same token.|Rewrite Git history before revoking the exposed credential.|Post the token into an issue so reviewers can confirm it.

65|A configured Semgrep rule always scans ignored directories.|A missing finding proves the unsafe source is secure.|Repository layout changes cannot change scan coverage.|Add more rules while keeping the affected directory excluded.|Disable the rule to avoid inconsistent reports.|Delete the unsafe fixture without restoring scan coverage.

66|Vault dynamic credentials remain valid forever after first issuance.|Restarting every application renews leases without Vault access.|A lease expiry is only a logging warning.|Cache expired credentials indefinitely.|Increase application retry rates without renewing credentials.|Distribute a permanent shared database password to bypass lease management.

67|A metadata constraint is a pod resource-scheduling error.|Admission rejection means Gatekeeper cannot read the image registry.|An owner label is automatically inferred from the Git author.|Disable every admission constraint for the namespace.|Add a fake owner value unrelated to the responsible team.|Deploy directly by bypassing the intended admission boundary.

68|Any valid cryptographic signature is trusted regardless of its identity.|A mutable image tag guarantees the same signed artifact forever.|Image signature failures are repaired by increasing pod CPU.|Allow every signature identity as trusted.|Disable verification for the production namespace.|Deploy an unreviewed digest solely because its tag looks familiar.

69|Every interactive shell alert is harmless by definition.|The shell can be explained solely by a high CPU metric.|Runtime alerts prove the application needs more replicas.|Delete the alert and assume the session is authorized.|Destroy all logs before investigating the container.|Grant every user exec permission to normalize the alert pattern.

70|Eviction always means Redis has exhausted its disk rather than memory.|Cache item size cannot affect memory demand.|A low hit rate is fixed by making every key permanent.|Remove all TTLs while leaving memory capacity unchanged.|Retry every missed lookup indefinitely against the database.|Disable eviction alerts without changing capacity or item footprint.

71|A waiting exclusive lock proves the migration SQL has invalid syntax.|PostgreSQL ignores open transactions during schema changes.|More migration retries automatically release another transaction's locks.|Launch concurrent copies of the same blocking migration.|Terminate every database session without identifying the blocker.|Disable lock monitoring and let the migration wait indefinitely.

72|An asynchronous replica guarantees every read sees the latest write.|Increasing client retry counts makes unapplied replication events visible.|Replica lag is measured by the application's image tag.|Send all freshness-sensitive reads to the stale replica.|Promote the lagging replica without a failover review.|Ignore lag and declare correctness based only on a successful connection.

73|Every rebalance is caused by insufficient topic replication.|Processing time cannot affect consumer group membership.|A consumer can stop polling indefinitely and retain its assignment.|Increase batch sizes without reviewing processing time.|Commit offsets before processing as a universal fix.|Raise retry frequency while retaining the oversized blocking batches.

74|Unacknowledged messages consume no consumer memory.|Unlimited prefetch is equivalent to unlimited processing capacity.|Consumer acknowledgements are sent only when the queue is deleted.|Acknowledge every message before processing it regardless of delivery needs.|Set unlimited worker concurrency to match unlimited prefetch.|Drop unacknowledged messages without business reconciliation.

75|An image rollback automatically restores dropped database columns.|The old image is compatible because it passed its original build.|Scaling old pods alone reverses the schema migration.|Roll back only the image and assume schema compatibility.|Recreate the database from scratch without assessing live data.|Apply another destructive migration before establishing serving compatibility.

76|Failed state persistence proves no cloud resources changed.|Deleting the backend automatically reconstructs exact state.|A force-unlock repairs missing backend write permissions.|Delete the backend state and rerun the full apply.|Discard preserved recovery state and import random resources.|Force concurrent applies before restoring authorized state persistence.

77|Kubernetes Ready alone proves critical user transactions succeed.|An ALB error always means the certificate must be replaced.|The database is healthy because the local stub returns 200.|Increase pod count while every pod has the same invalid database access.|Replace end-to-end checks with the local stub permanently.|Disable ALB health checks to hide the failed serving path.

78|A network partition proves the old writer cannot accept any writes.|An asynchronous replica is always current enough for lossless promotion.|DNS failover automatically fences the original database writer.|Promote the lagging replica and send writes to both regions.|Switch DNS before deciding which database is authoritative.|Discard replication-position evidence and promise zero data loss.

79|A manual kubectl rollback changes Git's desired image automatically.|Argo CD self-heal never reverses manual Deployment changes.|Repeated rollback failure proves the image registry is offline.|Repeat the live rollback without changing desired state.|Delete healthy replicas to slow reconciliation.|Disable all GitOps permanently instead of using the recovery procedure.

80|Silenced application alerts prove the services are healthy.|Maintenance inhibition cannot outlive its original maintenance window.|A zone failure is resolved by changing dashboard colors.|Silence the independent service probes too.|Delete the maintenance label while leaving its broad inhibition rule unexamined.|Suppress every alert until application owners notice the outage manually.

81|Restarting all pods preserves their in-memory usable credentials.|A running pod's valid credential instantly expires when Vault is unavailable.|A Vault outage makes every existing serving pod unsafe to retain.|Restart all healthy pods before restoring secret issuance.|Revoke every still-valid credential during the outage without replacement capacity.|Disable secret authorization and publish fallback passwords.

82|Kafka offset commits automatically roll back external database transactions.|Consumer retries guarantee exactly one external side effect.|A successful transaction prevents its source event from being replayed.|Commit offsets before processing and accept unnoticed data loss.|Replay all payment events without durable deduplication.|Delete duplicate records without reconciling external payment effects.

83|A healthy cache endpoint proves a cold cache cannot overload a database.|Every cache miss should trigger unlimited immediate backend retries.|Scaling callers always improves a saturated shared backend.|Scale every caller immediately without bounding database demand.|Expire all remaining cache keys at once.|Retry every expensive cache fill concurrently without coalescing.

84|Healthy EC2 nodes guarantee unlimited pod IP availability.|Pod IP allocation is controlled only by container memory limits.|A missing pod IP proves the image tag is invalid.|Restart every CNI pod without adding or releasing address capacity.|Scale out more nodes into the already exhausted subnet without reviewing demand.|Assign arbitrary static pod IPs outside the supported CNI allocation design.

85|Trusting a new CA on servers automatically updates every client trust store.|A valid server certificate is accepted by clients that do not trust its issuer.|Random TLS failures prove every certificate has expired.|Remove the old CA from every client before trust overlap is established.|Disable verification on all internal clients permanently.|Rotate all servers again without updating client trust bundles.

86|Telemetry volume stays constant when application retries multiply.|Per-customer metric labels always have bounded cardinality.|An overloaded monitoring backend means user traffic must be healthy.|Increase telemetry labels and sample every retry in full.|Drop every health signal while retaining verbose debug traces.|Make collector buffers unbounded instead of limiting telemetry pressure.

87|A PDB creates replacement capacity automatically.|A drain command guarantees safe evacuation even when no replacement can run.|Ready replicas concentrated in one zone provide zone-loss resilience.|Force-delete every protected pod before creating replacement capacity.|Set the PDB to allow total unavailability without incident review.|Drain all nodes in the zone simultaneously and hope rescheduling succeeds.

88|A mutable latest tag is identical to the digest scanned earlier.|A passed build authorizes every future artifact with the same tag.|Signature verification can ignore the deployed image identity.|Deploy the current latest tag without checking its digest.|Rescan a different digest and reuse the old approval.|Trust only the tag spelling rather than artifact provenance.

89|An existing backup object proves it is decryptable by recovery operators.|S3 object replication automatically restores a deleted KMS key.|A backup checksum alone proves restore permissions exist.|Schedule deletion of all old keys before rehearsing restore.|Grant public bucket access to repair missing KMS decrypt authorization.|Re-encrypt nothing and declare recovery complete after listing object names.

90|Two infrastructure controllers automatically share field ownership safely.|The newest apply permanently disables all other reconcilers.|A resource's tags guarantee its management ownership.|Run both conflicting applies faster until they converge.|Delete the live security group to settle the ownership dispute.|Ignore drift from both tools while claiming a single desired state.

91|DNS uses UDP only in every valid response path.|A successful small DNS lookup proves TCP fallback works.|Blocking TCP port 53 cannot affect large DNS responses.|Allow all egress to fix a narrowly scoped DNS transport issue.|Increase DNS retry counts while retaining the blocked transport.|Switch to arbitrary external DNS servers outside the approved network design.

92|Retries add no downstream load during partial failure.|Unbounded concurrency always helps a recovering database.|Increasing timeout alone removes synchronized retry traffic.|Retry every failed request immediately without a budget.|Raise Lambda concurrency while RDS remains saturated.|Remove caller deadlines and queue work without bounds.

93|Organization-wide OIDC trust is equivalent to repository-specific production trust.|A trusted issuer guarantees every subject is authorized for production.|Short-lived tokens make overly broad trust harmless.|Trust every repository and environment to avoid deployment failures.|Replace federated identity with a shared permanent administrator key.|Restrict only the workflow display name while allowing unauthorized subjects.

94|Restarting every system simultaneously is the safest compound recovery.|A healthy backup-region connection proves replication is current and writers are fenced.|Independent uncoordinated repairs cannot interfere with one another.|Promote every database replica and route writes to all of them.|Let conflicting automation continue while restarting all healthy capacity.|Roll back only the image without checking schema, replication or desired-state compatibility.
